what_its_for: Urea 40.5% cream is used to soften, loosen, and remove thick, rough, dry, or scaly skin. It is commonly used to treat conditions like very dry skin, cracked heels, calluses, corns, eczema, psoriasis, and thickened nails. Urea works by breaking down the protein in the outer layer of skin, helping to moisturize and soften the affected area.
how_to_take: Use this cream on your skin only — do not swallow it or get it in your eyes, nose, or mouth. Wash and dry the affected area before applying the cream. Apply a thin layer of cream to the affected skin and rub it in gently until it is absorbed. Wash your hands after applying the cream unless you are treating your hands. Do not cover the treated area with a tight bandage or wrap unless your doctor tells you to. Use it exactly as directed by your doctor or as stated on the label.
dosing: Apply the cream to the affected area 1 to 2 times per day, or as directed by your doctor. Do not use more cream than recommended, and do not use it more often than instructed. Your doctor may adjust how often you use it based on how your skin responds to treatment.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular routine. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store this cream at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep the cream away from heat, direct sunlight, and freezing temperatures. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the cream after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting this cream in your eyes, ears, nose, or mouth. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. Avoid applying the cream to broken, irritated, infected, or inflamed skin unless your doctor specifically tells you to do so. Avoid using on skin that has a rash or open wound. Do not use other skin products, lotions, or medications on the same area without checking with your doctor first. Avoid tight clothing or bandages over the treated area unless instructed by your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: signs of a skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, or pus; severe skin irritation, burning, stinging, or peeling that does not go away; an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; your skin condition gets worse or does not improve after a few weeks of use. Call your doctor if you have any questions or concerns about how the cream is working.
when_it_works: Many people notice their skin beginning to feel softer and smoother within a few days of starting treatment. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks or longer to see the full benefit, especially for thicker or more stubborn skin conditions. Be patient and keep using the cream as directed. If you do not see any improvement after 2 to 4 weeks, talk to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using this cream to make sure it is safe for them and their baby. This cream should be used in children only under the direction of a doctor, as children's skin may be more sensitive. Elderly patients may have more sensitive skin and should use the cream carefully to avoid irritation. People with kidney problems should let their doctor know before using products containing urea, especially over large areas of skin.
